input.question: If the coriolis effect makes hurricanes/typhoons swirl in different directions, what exactly happens when storms cross the equator? Do they begin to slow and weaken?
input.ground_truth: Look at [this chart](_URL_0_). Hurricanes don't cross the equator! They don't even form very close to the equator, because the Coriolis effect doesn't exist at the equator and is very small at small latitudes. As a storm approaches the equator, it either loses intensity or turns away because there is no driving force there to keep it going.

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine the Earth is like a big, spinning top. When the Earth spins, it makes the air move in a special way called the "Coriolis effect." This is like when you swirl water in a bathtub and it goes in a circle.

Now, hurricanes and typhoons (which are just big, swirling storms) spin in circles. But here’s the funny thing: in the **Northern Hemisphere** (like the top part of the Earth), they spin one way—let’s say, clockwise if you’re looking down from space, but actually it’s counterclockwise! In the **Southern Hemisphere** (the bottom part), they spin the other way.

Now, if one of these big storms is spinning in the Northern Hemisphere and it crosses the **equator** (that’s the imaginary line right in the middle of the Earth), something interesting happens!

When the storm crosses the equator, it suddenly finds itself in the Southern Hemisphere. The Coriolis effect now makes the air move the *opposite* way! So the storm has to "flip" its spinning direction. It’s like if you were jumping from a merry-go-round going one way to another one going the opposite way—you’d have to turn around!

But does the storm get slower or weaker? Not always. Sometimes the storm can keep its strength, but it does have to change the way it spins. It’s a bit like when you try to walk straight but suddenly the ground changes direction under your feet—you might stumble, but you don’t always get weaker.

So, when a storm crosses the equator, it changes the way it spins, but it doesn’t always get weaker or slower. It just starts twirling the other way!
